metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Iowa (2026): Rules, Exemptions & Examples

description: Iowa has statewide sales tax, but bullion is fully exempt. Many metal-value coins may qualify; jewelry is taxable. No purchase threshold applies.

What's covered by the exemption
Bullion and many coins valued by metal content
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Even when the state-level rule is clear, cities or counties in this state may charge their own tax. Here's what to expect.
Local treatment
Local option tax generally follows state rule
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Iowa.
Is gold and silver bullion taxable in Iowa?
+
No. Iowa treats bullion as fully exempt from sales tax under its investment metal-content treatment.
Are coins sales-tax exempt in Iowa?
+
Many coins valued primarily for their metal content can be exempt, but numismatic/collectible treatment can be conditional depending on the item.
Do I pay sales tax on numismatic coins in Iowa?
+
Sometimes. Iowa’s exemption is strongest for bullion and coins valued mainly by metal content, while collectible/numismatic pieces may be conditional.
Is jewelry taxable in Iowa?
+
Yes. Jewelry is taxable even though bullion and many covered investment-style coins are exempt.
Do local Iowa taxes change the bullion exemption?
+
Generally no. Local option tax typically follows the state rule, so exempt bullion remains exempt.
